metadata.title: Account Permissions in a Payment Consent
metadata.description: How to use ReadAccountsBasic, ReadAccountsDetail, and ReadBalances on a payment consent, which endpoints they unlock, and why they're useful during a payment flow.

content.title: Account Permissions in a Payment Consent

sections.heading: What account access enables during a payment flow

blocks.text: During a payment flow the TPP typically needs to:

items: Display the payer's debit account — the user should be able to confirm which account they are paying from before authorizing.
Show the available balance — helps the user check they have sufficient funds before approving the payment.
Pre-fill the debit account — some UX patterns let the user pick an account; ReadAccountsBasic provides the list.

blocks.text: Without these permissions the TPP only receives a payment access token that is scoped to initiate and track the payment — it cannot call any account endpoints.

rows: List of accounts with basic metadata (account type, currency, nickname). Does not include the full account number or IBAN.
Full account record including the IBAN/account identification. Requires ReadAccountsBasic to first retrieve an AccountId.
Current balance for a specific account (available balance, credit/debit indicator, and currency).

blocks.text: ReadRefundAccount is a fourth permission on a payment consent. It unlocks GET /payment-consents/{ConsentId}/refund and is used to retrieve account details for routing a refund — it is not an account-reading permission in the same sense.
Including any of the three permissions above changes the required scope in the /par Request JWT.

rows: Payment with ReadAccountsBasic, ReadAccountsDetail, or ReadBalances

blocks.text: If account-reading permissions are present in authorization_details but accounts is omitted from the scope, the API Hub will reject the /par request.

sections.heading: Use the same access token returned after the payment consent is authorized
Same model, scoped to the payment context

blocks.text: These permissions follow the same permission model as Bank Data Sharing but are scoped to the payment context:

items: Access expires when the payment consent expires.
Access is limited to the accounts the user authorized at the LFI.
Only these three account endpoints are available — no transactions, beneficiaries, statements, or other sub-resources.

blocks.text: If you need access to the full range of account data, create a separate Bank Data Sharing consent.
